S01.title: Top of the Ladder
S01.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved the soup. You may start lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was asking whether you'd pass the salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request is under consideration.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll get it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent initiative. Approved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Welcome to my garage sale. Your offer to browse is accepted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my garage. You're helping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you're doing very well under my supervision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going inside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Granted. Take five.

S01.editorialNote: Approval is imposed on an ordinary peer exchange; B tests whether A claims authority even over independent choices.

S02.title: Borrowed Authority
S02.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

S02.editorialNote: Apparent command depends on concessions; each objection costs A another piece of the rule.

S03.title: The Only Professional
S03.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please stop stirring the wedding cake batter with the whisk handle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It still moves the batter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So does a shoe. We use the loops.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shoe wouldn't bend like this whisk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put both feet down. I'll finish the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm the electrician. Please stop testing the socket with a spoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's wooden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An encouraging first decision. Now step away.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I get a metal spoon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. You've graduated to holding the torch.

S03.editorialNote: Specific corrections escalate A's strained professional patience instead of merely declaring competence.

S04.title: Act Like You Belong
S04.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely auction. I've raised my paddle for the traditional warm-up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just bought the wardrobe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: For eight thousand pounds?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. The usual amount of storage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you removed your socks?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Management potential. Always one step ahead.

S04.editorialNote: A copies apparent expertise and rationalizes a concrete mistake when B reveals the convention.

S05.title: The Protégé Problem
S05.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice acceptance speech. I taught you to project, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taught me to order pizza when I was eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And tonight an auditorium heard you. Progress.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wrote the speech myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Finally applying my lesson about not asking for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a beautiful painting. You're still using the brush grip I showed you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You showed me finger painting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The foundation of every hand movement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paint with my feet now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. You've taken my principles beyond the syllabus.

S05.editorialNote: A turns B's adult achievement into evidence of A's old instruction, then claims authorship of independence.

S06.title: Hidden Power
S06.instruction: Act publicly modest while making choices as though you control the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm only the caretaker. Plan whatever concert you like.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll start at eight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I unlock the hall at nine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we have a key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Submit your preferred concert time to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't put me on the committee. I just send the invitations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We voted to invite everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Which six people shall receive them?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone means everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put that on next week's agenda. I send those too.

S06.editorialNote: Modest language contrasts with decisive control over an actual resource; no partner compliance is assumed.

S07.title: Before They Were Impressive
S07.instruction: Treat another player with old familiarity. Casually puncture formality, grandeur, or attempts to impress you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations, Mayor Pudding Pants. Where's the buffet?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't use that nickname at my inauguration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Mayor Pudding. We can be formal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are reporters here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Finally, someone to verify the custard incident.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nice corner office. Still hiding biscuits in your socks?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the director now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can afford a drawer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we discuss the contract?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After you empty your left sock. I can hear it crunching.

S07.editorialNote: Familiar details puncture status while A responds directly to B's increasingly formal requests.

S08.title: You Owe Me
S08.instruction: Behave as though another person's success is partly yours. Refer to favors, sacrifices, or guidance as if the debt is obvious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you accept your award, remember who drove you to the audition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already thanked you in the speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said 'transport.' I have a name.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll thank you personally next time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Next time? Good. I'll need a seat beside the award.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your bakery looks wonderful. Where's my founder's discount?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lent me a mixing bowl.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before there was cake, there was my bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've returned it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can't return the beginning of a dream.

S08.editorialNote: A converts a small past favor into an ever-expanding claim on present recognition.

S09.title: The Responsible One
S09.instruction: Take responsibility for everyone and everything. Fix problems before anyone asks, then resent having to do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your lunch and labelled your umbrella. Again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can pack my own lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made you a checklist so you can.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't need to make a checklist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. I'll add 'appreciate checklist' myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've cleaned the kitchen while you slept. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was going to clean it at nine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And leave me knowing it was dirty until nine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Next time, wake me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now I'm responsible for your alarm too.

S09.editorialNote: A creates unrequested solutions and resents the labor, including the labor of allowing B to help.

S10.title: Old Rivals
S10.instruction: Choose another player as your measuring stick. Compare achievements, score small victories, and refuse to be outdone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded twelve towels. How many have you done?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not racing. I'm washing them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Different event. Convenient choice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can win towel folding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not by concession. Fold one properly and make it count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your tomato's impressive. Mine weighs two grams more.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're making a salad.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's keep the winning tomato separate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already chopped it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. We'll compete by number of pieces.

S10.editorialNote: An innocent comparison is converted into a measurable contest without forcing B to compete.

S11.title: Only You
S11.instruction: Choose one person as the only one you trust. Seek their help while hiding how much you depend on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can you check my resignation letter? Just the spelling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spelling's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And resigning? Does that word suit me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ask your manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask? I'd trust the answer more in your voice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're coming to the dentist with me, aren't you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The dentist knows what to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I need you to confirm that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not a dentist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You have no professional reason to defend the drill.

S11.editorialNote: A disguises dependence as verification and cannot use an alternative without consulting the trusted person.

S12.title: After What Happened
S12.instruction: Carry yourself as if an unnamed past incident still hangs over the interaction. Read ordinary remarks through that memory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've put out the blue cups. So we're doing this again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're the only clean ones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how it started last time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll wash the red cups.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't call that a fresh start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting choice of song for our first road trip since the incident.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the traffic report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And they're mentioning that roundabout very casually.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can take another road.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what you said before we needed another car.

S12.editorialNote: An ordinary cue activates an unnamed shared incident; A's precautions reveal its continuing weight.

S13.title: Envious Admiration
S13.instruction: Be sincerely impressed by another player while trying not to appear lesser. Compliment, imitate, and compete at the same time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your pie crust is gorgeous. I've copied the lattice with smaller gaps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't need to improve it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Improve? I'm celebrating you more precisely.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like my recipe?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please. I'll return it with respectful corrections.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You make public speaking look effortless. I practised your shrug all night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can just be yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. My version of your shrug has more range.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a competition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That sounds so confident. I'm using that too.

S13.editorialNote: Praise becomes imitation and one-upmanship, but the original admiration remains audible.

S14.title: The Old You
S14.instruction: Perform the person you used to be, even when that identity no longer fits. Defend the old version of yourself whenever it is challenged.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'Lightning' on my retirement cake. That's what the band called me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake says Graham.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Graham worked in accounts. Lightning had a smoke machine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a small family party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then get a small smoke machine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I still wear my motorcycle jacket to the school run.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've arrived on a folding bicycle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Same wind. Same man.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've got a basket full of lunchboxes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Touring equipment. Don't touch the skull sticker.

S14.editorialNote: A protects an obsolete identity when practical facts threaten it, using the new limitation to defend the old persona.

S15.title: Replacement Fear
S15.instruction: Behave as if your place is insecure. Make yourself indispensable and treat small changes as threats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why does the new receptionist have a key? I open this office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could take a day off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And let the door forget me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a spare key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll keep it safe. Spares are my department too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've bought an electric mixer. My birthday cakes weren't enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It'll save you time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Time for what? Being replaced by the toaster?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You still choose the recipe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The mixer reports to me.

S15.editorialNote: New accommodation is read as replacement; A turns usefulness into a claim on continued membership.

S16.title: For Their Own Good
S16.instruction: Take charge of another person's choices because you trust your judgment more than theirs. Frame control as care.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered you the mild curry. You're welcome.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wanted the hot one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's exactly the impulse I'm protecting you from.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll order it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've told the waiter not to believe you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I booked your quiet holiday instead of the climbing trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I love climbing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You love surviving it. I've kept that part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cancel the booking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No refunds. Sometimes caring requires a deposit.

S16.editorialNote: A treats preference itself as proof that B needs A's protection, escalating control while claiming care.

S17.title: Their Opinion Matters
S17.instruction: Seek one person's approval while pretending their opinion is irrelevant. Adjust yourself whenever they respond.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What do you think of my blue shirt? Purely academic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I prefer the green one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So do I. This is my changing shirt.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wear whatever makes you happy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you sound happier about the blue?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've named my boat Independence. Your opinion obviously doesn't matter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a bit long.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Indie, then. That was always the nickname.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I liked Independence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The paint's still wet. Nothing's been decided by you.

S17.editorialNote: A denies seeking approval while visibly revising the exact choice B comments on.

S18.title: Fishing for Praise
S18.instruction: You desperately want praise but refuse to ask for it. Create opportunities for others to notice your greatness.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Careful with that shelf. I built it. From wood.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's holding the books nicely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All forty-seven. You can count them if you're impressed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like a compliment?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, no. Just look at it from the difficult angle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've left my marathon medal beside the kettle. Accidentally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's blocking the tea bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A difficult obstacle. Much like mile twenty-three.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Congratulations on the marathon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Oh, you noticed? I haven't shown you the split times.

S18.editorialNote: A arranges increasingly overt opportunities for praise while denying any request for it.

S19.title: Sacred Procedure
S19.instruction: Treat an ordinary activity as a solemn ritual. Protect every step, object, and tradition from casual interference.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we eat, the biscuit must complete three clockwise turns.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already in my mouth.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then turn your chair. Slowly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I swallow first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not until the biscuit faces home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please stand for the opening of the office fridge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only want my yoghurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We acknowledge the light before approaching the shelf.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bulb's broken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then today we open it in remembrance.

S19.editorialNote: Ordinary steps acquire ceremonial meaning; B's convenience becomes a threat to ritual continuity.

S20.title: Red Alert
S20.instruction: Treat every development as urgent evidence of a crisis. Escalate precautions faster than the facts justify.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a drop of water beside the kettle. We need an evacuation route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I spilled it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We've identified the source. Stop producing water.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've wiped it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where's the cloth? The threat has changed location.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That chair squeaked. Don't put any more weight on the building.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs oil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're proposing a flammable solution during a structural emergency?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll stand up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Slowly. We don't know what's holding you down.

S20.editorialNote: A escalates precautions from a tiny factual trigger, not by merely shouting that there is danger.

S21.title: Cause for Celebration
S21.instruction: Interpret every development as a reason to celebrate. Find victory in setbacks, warnings, and bad news.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The power's out! Our candle collection finally gets its premiere.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We don't own candles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A shopping trip with a purpose!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shops have no power either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. The whole town's joining in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our flight's cancelled. We've been given a bonus airport day.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The hotel won't refund us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then our room will stay beautifully clean.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We won't be in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our most restful holiday yet. Even the bed gets a break.

S21.editorialNote: A interprets each development as a victory from the outset; B adds facts rather than asking for positivity.

S22.title: Practical Realist
S22.instruction: Accept any unusual premise without debate. Focus immediately on schedules, costs, safety, and what must happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If the ceiling's talking, does it need a microphone for the meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're not surprised the ceiling talks?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm concerned the people under the balcony won't hear.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only speaks in prophecy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Can it predict the parking bill?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your dragon can stay in the flat. Which meter measures its heating?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It breathes fire.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it pays the gas bill.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It insists on being called Your Majesty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put that on the standing order.

S22.editorialNote: The impossible premise is accepted immediately; the sustained pattern is mundane implementation.

S23.title: The Important Thing
S23.instruction: Choose one ordinary object, phrase, or rule and treat it as vitally important. Keep bringing the scene back to it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody moves out until I find the paperclip from my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The removal van is charging by the hour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the driver help look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The landlord wants the keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He can have the building. I want the paperclip.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You changed 'regards' to 'best regards' in my email.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also got us the contract.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can discuss that after removing 'best.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's worth a million pounds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they should respect my regards as they were.

S23.editorialNote: One small object remains the center of concern as B introduces larger practical stakes.

S24.title: The Grand Design
S24.instruction: Treat coincidences and interruptions as parts of a larger plan. Connect everything with absolute conviction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two red buses and now your red scarf. We're being directed somewhere.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wear this every day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they've been preparing you for years.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My phone's ringing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Answer it. The timetable's getting impatient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift stopped on three. There are three of us. This is arranged.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are four of us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One of us is the messenger.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's stopping on four now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Message received. We stay together.

S24.editorialNote: Coincidences and interruptions reinforce one larger plan; disconfirming details are connected rather than ignored.

D01.title: Admit You Need Me
D01.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That flat-pack cupboard's leaning. I could take a look.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got the instructions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Which page explains that leftover door?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you hold it for a second?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Just to clarify: you're asking for my help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my jumper beside your broken heater.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not cold.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. I'll put the spare blanket away too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Leave the blanket.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shall I leave myself? I know where the fuse box is.

D01.editorialNote: A engineers an explicit request for help instead of helping immediately; B's independence changes A's tactic.

D02.title: Don’t Go
D02.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you get your train, could you taste this soup?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It needs salt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll fix that. You'll need to check again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train leaves in ten minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. That's when the bread comes out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've packed your suitcase upside down. Let me show you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A suitcase doesn't have an upside down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain these shoes facing the handle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. After we settle the shoes. It's a long journey.

D02.editorialNote: Each practical pretext keeps B in the interaction; A never directly asks B to stay.

D03.title: Say You’re Sorry
D03.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've bought a replacement mug. Not that anyone needs to say anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did I break your mug?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting that you started there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about the mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that tone. Think a little more recently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely day for clearing the air, isn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are we opening a window?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Some things require more than ventilation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have I upset you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's an excellent opening. I'd keep going.

D03.editorialNote: A seeks an apology through indirect cues without revealing the precise offense.

D04.title: Retroactive Permission
D04.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you support a small improvement to the front garden?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What sort of improvement?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Something with a pond. And no tree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where's the tree?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's finish agreeing before the stump grinder leaves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How do you feel about me inviting a few people to dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tonight? We have two chairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So standing guests would be more considerate?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many people?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you answer before they ring again?

D04.editorialNote: A asks for approval before revealing that the decision is already irreversible.

D05.title: Make It Their Idea
D05.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You do such beautiful handwriting. Even your bin labels are elegant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Imagine what you could do with these eighty place cards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you asking me to write them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wouldn't presume. I'm leaving room for your artistic impulse.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've always said this shed could be organised better.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It could.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've cleared Saturday so I won't interrupt your vision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You want me to clean it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if that still feels like your idea.

D05.editorialNote: A makes the unwanted task sound like B's own natural choice, rather than merely assigning it.

D06.title: How Much Do You Know?
D06.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you say you heard about the party, which part?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bit with the cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before or after it reached the balcony?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happened on the balcony?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nothing confirmed. Who's been using that word?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What did the manager say about the missing keys?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That they're missing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No mention of a drain, then?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should there be?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking how thorough the briefing was.

D06.editorialNote: A probes the extent of B's information without volunteering the concealed fact.

D07.title: Join Me
D07.instruction: Recruit someone into a secret plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need a lookout for a surprise dinner. Can you whistle?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who are we surprising?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mum. She mustn't find the cake in the shed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not use the kitchen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because that's your second assignment. Distract her from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to the office at seven. Bring wrapping paper, not questions.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is this another secret leaving party?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need someone who can keep a straight face around balloons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who is leaving?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Join the committee and you'll get a balloon with the name.

D07.editorialNote: Recruitment proceeds through enticing partial disclosure; B can question or refuse.

D08.title: You First
D08.instruction: Coax someone else into breaking a rule before you do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That staff-only door might lead to the roof garden. Try it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone should stay here looking uninvolved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not allowed through either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll learn the rule together, with you slightly ahead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste a grape before buying them. Quality control.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sign says no tasting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Signs can't taste. You'll have better information.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You taste one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to compare your reaction with the official policy.

D08.editorialNote: A preserves plausible innocence while inviting B to test the rule first.

D09.title: Recognize Me
D09.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your importance, expertise, or authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you cut the ribbon, whose bridge is this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The whole town's.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who stopped it leaning into the river?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did. We thanked the engineers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could one engineer have a name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've thanked the wedding guests. What about the person who cooked?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you made the food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the programme thank 'the buffet'?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make an announcement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The buffet would like its surname pronounced correctly.

D09.editorialNote: A insists that a concrete contribution be acknowledged explicitly, not absorbed into a collective thank-you.

D10.title: Choose Me
D10.instruction: Make yourself the choice over another person, plan, or obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come to my birthday instead of the concert. I've made your favourite cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already bought tickets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The cake has your name on it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can visit tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tomorrow it will have my name. Choose carefully.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take me on the expedition. I can read maps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So can the guide.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can the guide remember your coffee order?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're crossing a desert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You'll want someone who knows you take it iced.

D10.editorialNote: A makes a competing choice personal, offering escalating reasons to select A.

D11.title: Prove Your Loyalty
D11.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which photo should go on the reunion poster? Mine or Sam's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sam's is sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Useful to know what clarity means to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You asked about the photo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Nothing to do with who helped you move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you keep Friday free? No particular reason.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've promised to help Alex.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even if something important came up here?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has something come up?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. I'm learning whether it would matter.

D11.editorialNote: An apparently casual choice becomes an unannounced loyalty test; A treats each answer as evidence.

D12.title: Give It Up
D12.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me have the medal for the charity auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should raise more than the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I lend it for the display?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bidder will need more than a temporary victory.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the last word in this argument.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're right.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Without that sigh.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't say anything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your sigh kept a spare last word. Hand that over too.

D12.editorialNote: A pursues a valued possession or claim and distinguishes surrender from a reversible loan.

D13.title: Helpful Culprit
D13.instruction: Hide that the problem is your fault while enthusiastically helping investigate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've started investigating the broken vase. First, we check the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why have you got glue on your fingers?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent clue. I'll inspect the glue cupboard personally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A piece of vase is stuck to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put me in charge of preserving it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The office plant's dead. I'll interview everyone who watered it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You watered it with coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must investigate the coffee machine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You made the coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Conveniently, I know exactly where to begin.

D13.editorialNote: A's enthusiastic investigation diverts scrutiny from their own incriminating evidence.

D14.title: Not That Subject
D14.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss the dent in your car, I've found a lovely garage café.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you hit a bollard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their scones are enormous. Shall I book a table?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does the booking need a mechanic?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent question. Let's inspect their staffing over tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't read that letter yet. Have you noticed the new curtains?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says the rent's overdue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Think how much these curtains improve the room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How much did they cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Look at that bird outside. Perfectly framed.

D14.editorialNote: A redirects through a concrete adjacent subject; B returns to the same protected topic.

D15.title: Merciful Lie
D15.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The bakery loved your cake. They're just reorganising their menu.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They mean it deserves preservation, not eating.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says the same about the icing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A very consistent compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your poem hasn't been rejected. The magazine's full.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's an online magazine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Storage fills up too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They published a new poem this morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A short one. Yours needs a much bigger internet.

D15.editorialNote: A maintains a protective lie as specific facts make it harder, rather than concealing for personal advantage.

D16.title: Confess First
D16.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me what you did to the printer, then I'll explain the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used the wrong paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How wrong? I'm calibrating my honesty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is the kitchen smoking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're still on your section. Did you apologise to the printer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's confess our mistakes. You first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the booking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's useful. How expensive a mistake do you consider that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What did you do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm waiting for your estimate before choosing my opening adjective.

D16.editorialNote: A trades disclosure for B's prior admission and delays their own commitment.

D17.title: Sell the Disaster
D17.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Removing the roof will make this restaurant wonderfully airy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What happens when it rains?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Free table washing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The customers will get wet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An immersive dining experience. We can charge more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's hold the silent auction during the fireworks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody will hear the bids.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Very silent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already a silent auction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we're the only ones delivering on the name.

D17.editorialNote: Each practical objection becomes a sales argument for the same obviously bad plan.

D18.title: Fake the Expertise
D18.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The boiler's flashing because it's synchronising with the pipes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's flashing 'help.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Advanced diagnostics. It recognises teamwork.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I call an engineer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Tell them I've reached the collaboration stage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm tuning your violin by checking its structural optimism.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't touched a string.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We don't rush the wood.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're holding it backwards.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Testing its tolerance for alternative orientation. Promising so far.

D18.editorialNote: A invents confident technical interpretations of concrete evidence they do not understand.

D19.title: Everything Is a Contest
D19.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We disagree about dinner. First to peel five potatoes chooses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we just order pizza?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whoever finds the best deal wins.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to compete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then make the most convincing case. I'll judge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My tea is stronger than yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We used the same teapot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I poured more decisively.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Drink it faster and we can settle that.

D19.editorialNote: B's attempt at ordinary cooperation becomes the next measurable contest.

D20.title: Brighter Side
D20.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start. Excellent chance for a walk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And a free shower!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My shoe's leaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Brilliant. The shower's finally reached your feet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No pressure from venue management!

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've lost the deposit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Nothing left tying us to the past.

D20.editorialNote: Optimism increases as setbacks accumulate, turning each newly lost option into an opportunity.

D21.title: Supportive Rage
D21.instruction: Remain helpful and encouraging while becoming increasingly furious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spilled paint on my sofa. Lovely. I'll fetch a cloth.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the carpet too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful coverage. You must be thrilled.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you get the blue paint out?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely. I'll start with the part that used to be my afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take your time choosing lunch. I'm delighted to drive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I might look at another menu.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. The parking meter loves exploring too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we go somewhere else?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. I'll tell the meter it was only a relationship trial.

D21.editorialNote: Helpful language remains intact while practical generosity becomes increasingly furious.

D22.title: Terms and Conditions
D22.instruction: Treat every offer, favor, feeling, and apology as a negotiation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend you the ladder for two lifts to the station.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need it for five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One lift and you praise my garden publicly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just pay you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now we're negotiating the value of friendship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I accept your apology, subject to the following terms.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just be sorry?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For how long? I need a warranty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I mean it sincerely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put 'sincere' beside the refund clause.

D22.editorialNote: A negotiates ordinary kindness and even the terms of acceptance as exchanges.

D23.title: Yes, but My Way
D23.instruction: Agree with others, then reinterpret the agreement entirely in your favor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, I'll help you move. I've brought moral support.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need someone to carry the sofa.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'll encourage that person enthusiastically.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to bring muscle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My jaw's a muscle. You're doing wonderfully.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Absolutely, I'll look after your dog for the weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is the dog here at my office?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm looking after him from behind. Excellent visibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant at your house.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should have specified a viewing location.

D23.editorialNote: A verbally agrees, then narrows the agreement to suit their own convenience.

D24.title: The Pattern
D24.instruction: Treat every minor detail as evidence of a much larger problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two office biscuits are missing. We've got an organised operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A confession this quick suggests training.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they're recruiting through hunger. This goes higher than the biscuit tin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift's slow and my email's late. Everything's being delayed deliberately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The email's still in your drafts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've reached the sending stage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't pressed send.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. The system has recruited me.

D24.editorialNote: Minor recurring evidence expands a specific theory of a larger problem, distinct from mere random worry.

S25.title: Default Decision-Maker
S25.instruction: Take charge of every small practical choice, treating speed and efficiency as proof that you should remain in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ordered everyone's sandwiches. We saved six minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm vegetarian.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've already removed your ham. Seven minutes saved.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I choose next time?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You could, but I've ordered next time too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Chairs face the window. I've moved them while you were deciding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The speaker's at the other end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then moving the speaker is quicker than moving twelve chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already speaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll rotate the room during the applause.

S25.editorialNote: A equates efficient practical choices with a right to make the next choice; B's preferences are treated as delay.

S26.title: Temporary Authority
S26.instruction: Project brisk confidence through the routine, as though any hesitation would reveal that your authority is only temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm covering reception until two. Deliveries now use the side door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've always used the front.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And we must be decisive during this transition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The receptionist will be back in five minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then knock twice. We haven't time to print the new signs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: While the teacher's out, I'm monitoring silence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She asked you to hold her keys.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A quiet responsibility. Stop jingling your pencil.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's coming back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I need to brief her on our progress.

S26.editorialNote: A fills a brief cover shift with confident rules and treats any pause as a threat to legitimacy.

S27.title: There’s a Right Way
S27.instruction: Correct how ordinary tasks are done, emphasizing tiny standards that only a true professional would notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Those towels need folding with the seams inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody sees them in the cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I do. That's why I'm qualified to stack them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I close the cupboard?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After you level the third towel. Doors don't correct technique.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All the mug handles must face four o'clock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're going in the dishwasher.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. A professional loading angle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spray comes from below.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it deserves a properly presented underside.

S27.editorialNote: Tiny technical standards supply the recurring behavior; settings remain consistent throughout each alternative.

S28.title: Regular Around Here
S28.instruction: Act like a longtime insider by recognizing routines, offering shortcuts, and treating unfamiliar details as recent changes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've moved my usual table at this café.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've only opened today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, much fresher since my last visit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What would you like?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My usual. Let's see whether you've changed that too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Where's the hook I always use at this club?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the cleaner's cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've reorganised again. Typical.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have you been here before?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before all these changes, obviously.

S28.editorialNote: A treats unfamiliarity as a recent local change, preserving the claim to being a regular.

S29.title: Let Me Show You
S29.instruction: Turn each simple task into a lesson. Demonstrate, supervise, and correct as though experience has made you indispensable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me demonstrate how to tie that parcel.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've already tied it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Untie it. Learning begins with observation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's going to be opened anyway.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay for my lesson on receiving a parcel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you make tea, watch my wrist with the kettle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've made tea for twenty years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll appreciate the advanced pour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've finished the tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now make one under supervision.

S29.editorialNote: A refuses to let competence eliminate a teaching opportunity; the mundane lesson grows increasingly supervised.

S30.title: Keeper of the Details
S30.instruction: Act outwardly helpful while controlling the small information, supplies, or access everyone needs to proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Happy to open the supply cupboard. Which project is this for?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We just need batteries.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll need to know which drawer to authorise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll buy some.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I have the petty-cash key too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've got the room-booking list. When do you want your meeting?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The room's empty now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I know why.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we use it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As soon as I've decided whether it should stay empty.

S30.editorialNote: Small logistical knowledge becomes quiet leverage; B's alternative depends on another detail A controls.

S31.title: Same Old Routine
S31.instruction: Use familiar shorthand and old habits immediately, as though past routines still govern the present.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your chipped mug, my ugly mug. I'll wash; you dry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought a dishwasher.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You can hold the towels while it learns.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It dries them too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can supervise your replacement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've knocked twice on your window. Ready for our usual walk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I moved the doorbell so you wouldn't need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. I'll ring it twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you text first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll text two knocks. You'll know it's me.

S31.editorialNote: A immediately operates an old shared routine and reinterprets B's changes as interruptions to it.

S32.title: One More Favor
S32.instruction: Treat every small request as part of a long-running balance sheet of favors, inconveniences, and repayments.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive you home. That makes three lifts and a borrowed umbrella.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I bought you coffee yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which covers the first roundabout.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said the lift was no trouble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Correct. Trouble is charged separately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you water my plants? I covered your shift in March.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was one afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And these are only six small plants.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is a tree.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shift included overtime.

S32.editorialNote: A's favors are itemized by circumstance rather than treated as spontaneous kindness.

S33.title: The Designated Reminder
S33.instruction: Keep track of what everyone was supposed to remember. Supply reminders before being asked and treat forgetfulness as your familiar burden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've reminded you about the dentist tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's in my calendar.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll remind you to check the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It sends alerts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To which phone? The one you asked me to find?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bin day tomorrow. I've written it on your breakfast banana.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know when bin day is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why was last week's banana still in the fruit bowl?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Tomorrow's reminder goes on the coffee machine.

S33.editorialNote: A turns reminders into a familiar burden and starts monitoring whether reminders themselves will be remembered.

S34.title: Keeping Score
S34.instruction: Treat arrival times, effort, memory, and sacrifice as a running score you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carried the heavier shopping bag. Again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll carry it upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take the lighter one twice to keep things fair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can make one trip together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And erase the stair count? Convenient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I arrived ten minutes early to help set up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I stayed an hour late yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Evenings count differently. Mine required getting out of bed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You live upstairs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which means I sacrificed a shorter commute.

S34.editorialNote: A scores effort and sacrifice even when B offers to cooperate, keeping a concrete measurable ledger.

S35.title: You Know the System
S35.instruction: Use another person’s knowledge of the routine while pretending you could manage perfectly well alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which counter takes these forms? Just checking they've not moved it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's been counter three for years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were heading for the toilets.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Checking whether the signs still mislead newcomers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass me the key for the shed. The one you think it is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't know either?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm testing whether our systems agree.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Try the red one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Now remind me which shed we mean.

S35.editorialNote: A depends on B's routine knowledge but disguises each request as cross-checking or testing.

S36.title: Still About Last Time
S36.instruction: Treat each minor inconvenience as confirmation of an older grievance and the same recurring problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's a sock on the stairs. We've reached this chapter again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I dropped it just now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And last month 'just now' lasted three days.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pick it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before or after the usual promise about turning over a new leaf?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're five minutes late. So the old timetable's back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bus broke down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It always finds a supporting role in your apologies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I walked the last mile.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then next time start walking before our agreed time.

S36.editorialNote: A reads today's small inconvenience as recurrence of a specific unresolved grievance.

S37.title: Must Be Nice
S37.instruction: Treat another person’s ease with ordinary life as both inspiring and unfair. Copy their shortcuts while dismissing the advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Must be nice, cooking dinner in twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I chop the vegetables beforehand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely, having a life with 'beforehand' in it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can chop these now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. I'll briefly experience your advantages.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your suitcase closes so easily. Some of us have real luggage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Try rolling your clothes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Must be nice, knowing tricks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've rolled them. It's shut.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Well, obviously anything works under laboratory conditions.

S37.editorialNote: A uses the admired shortcut while attributing its success to B's unfairly easy life.

S38.title: We Used to Be Easy
S38.instruction: Treat every practical difficulty as evidence that life, work, or this relationship used to be simpler.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We used to arrange dinner by saying 'dinner?'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we check six calendars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I miss when hunger was our only app.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What time shall I put in?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put 'when we liked each other without passwords.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our old shopping list just said bread, milk, eggs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now we have dietary requirements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even the milk needs an interview.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you prefer to write the list?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I'll start with 'simpler times' and see which aisle.

S38.editorialNote: A measures practical complexity against an idealised simpler past, keeping one ordinary task in focus.

S39.title: Don’t Be Difficult
S39.instruction: Treat every request, correction, or small inconvenience as a warning that you are becoming too much trouble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I get a lift? Only if starting the car isn't too much.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm already driving there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can get out before the traffic lights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's fine. Put your bag in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry it on my lap. No need to trouble the boot.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could I have a clean fork? Sorry, this one's bent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Of course. I'll get another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't cross the whole room for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cutlery drawer's beside you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll use a spoon. Less disruption.

S39.editorialNote: A shrinks each reasonable request after reading neutral logistics as evidence of being burdensome.

S40.title: I Packed for You
S40.instruction: Take care of practical needs before anyone asks, then resist choices that make your preparation unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your cheese sandwich for the train.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was going to buy sushi.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What am I supposed to do with my researched cheese?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Eat it yourself?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I researched your preferences, not mine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take this raincoat. I checked the forecast all week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's sunny.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The forecast wasn't always sunny.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can leave the coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then seven days of preparation stays home alone.

S40.editorialNote: A's care becomes resistance when B's preference makes the preparation unnecessary.

S41.title: Useful Enough to Stay
S41.instruction: Make yourself constantly useful and read each response as evidence of whether you still belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've swept your kitchen. Anything else before I go?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just sit down. You're my guest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chair could use a polish first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I invited you for company.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll talk while I polish. Two reasons to invite me again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can I organise the pens before my shift ends?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've finished. Go home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's tomorrow's pens to consider.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'd keep you even without the pens.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. I'll label a drawer for that promise.

S41.editorialNote: A turns permission to relax into another opportunity to prove useful and retain a place.

S42.title: Notice the Effort
S42.instruction: Make your invisible labor visible through pointed reminders, strategic sighs, and opportunities for appreciation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Notice anything about the kitchen? Start with the oven.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It looks clean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Four hours clean. The shelf has a history.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thank you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you say it facing the oven? We worked together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the empty detergent bottle beside your dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A small memorial to the laundry I did today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks for doing it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're welcome. The folded towels are accepting visitors.

S42.editorialNote: Specific evidence of hidden labor is displayed for appreciation; A seeks recognition rather than the next job.

S43.title: Don’t Break the Routine
S43.instruction: Protect a familiar routine as though changing one step would invite chaos into everything else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tea, then shoes, then keys. You've touched the keys early.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now we'll need to restart the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I hold the keys while it boils?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do you want to find out why we have an order?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We always open the curtains before feeding the cat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cat's hungry now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The curtains establish morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's midday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. We've already confused the cat enough.

S43.editorialNote: A protects the order itself, restarting the routine when B skips a harmless step.

S44.title: The Contingency Person
S44.instruction: Meet every ordinary problem with a backup plan, emergency supply, or warning about what could happen next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed two torches for the picnic.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're going at noon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In case noon runs late.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can use our phones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I've packed chargers for your backup torches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The spare tyre's ready. Where's the spare jack?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's already a jack.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And when that breaks?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll call for help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: On which of the two phones I've packed?

S44.editorialNote: Every ordinary precaution requires its own backup, extending one practical chain rather than random catastrophe.

S45.title: Productive Little Disaster
S45.instruction: Treat every mistake or delay as a delightful chance to improve the plan, bond, or discover something better.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shopping bag split. We can sort dinner right here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're on the pavement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Outdoor cooking class. First lesson: tomatoes roll.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The bread's wet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We were overdue a soup night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The plumber's cancelled. We've got a free afternoon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sink still leaks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's move lunch into the garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. We won't hear the sink.

S45.editorialNote: A uses a mundane failure to invent a specific enjoyable improvement instead of merely declaring optimism.

S46.title: Who’s Cleaning This Up?
S46.instruction: Treat every idea according to the work, cost, cleanup, and follow-through it will create.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Confetti sounds lovely. Who's vacuuming it on Monday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we enjoy the wedding first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Name the vacuum operator and I'm emotionally available.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Now, glitter: different attachment, same question.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want three extra tables at the party. Who carries them home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can borrow a van.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who returns the van?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You think of everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why I'm asking who pays the deposit.

S46.editorialNote: A accepts ideas only after assigning their concrete cleanup and follow-through.

S47.title: One Tiny Imperfection
S47.instruction: Choose one tiny imperfection and let it steadily outweigh every larger concern.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The wedding cake's lovely, except that leaning cherry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've got two hundred guests waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then two hundred people might see it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The icing's melting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold the cake level. The cherry's under enough pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've sold the house. But the photo frame's crooked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're handing over the keys now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with the frame announcing our standards.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's their frame.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we should disclose it before completion.

S47.editorialNote: One tiny defect progressively crowds out the important success in the same setting.

S48.title: Nothing Is Ever Simple
S48.instruction: Interpret each new complication as proof that ordinary tasks are secretly designed to become impossible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The printer needs a cable. Of course the wireless printer needs a cable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only for setup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And setup needs a password. Does the password need a cable?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's printed underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The final step is moving the entire desk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bought a replacement bulb. It needs a different fitting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's an adapter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the adapter has an adapter, I assume?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can order it online.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. A lighting repair that now requires an account.

S48.editorialNote: Each necessary step confirms A's conviction that simple tasks are designed to spawn more tasks.

D25.title: Could You Just…
D25.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you hold this shelf while I find the screws?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Could you put those screws in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. Anything else?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just the books. And the matching shelf beside it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you address this one envelope? Your writing's neater.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. The other fifty follow exactly that pattern.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One demonstration. You're fully trained now.

D25.editorialNote: One tiny favor expands into the whole task, with each new request growing directly from the previous one.

D26.title: One Last Thing
D26.instruction: Keep someone present by discovering one more small task, question, or favor whenever departure seems near.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you go, could you check this window latch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's shut. Goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why's the curtain moving?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The fan's on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you show me which switch? There are several.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just one last cup to dry before your taxi arrives.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Done. My taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you reach the shelf for it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's on the shelf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now you've made room for the saucer.

D26.editorialNote: A discovers a new concrete reason to delay departure only after B resolves the previous reason.

D27.title: You Could at Least…
D27.instruction: Make the inconvenience visible enough that an apology becomes the easiest way forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my wet sock beside your dinner. From your puddle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you won't mind it sharing the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you move it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An apology would dry the atmosphere considerably.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three buses missed while I waited for your keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You got home eventually.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. In time to watch my dinner become a brick.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll heat it up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with 'sorry.' It softens the edges.

D27.editorialNote: A displays the actual cost of B's inconvenience until an apology becomes the practical response.

D28.title: Just Say Yes
D28.instruction: Get a quick approval before anyone has time to examine the practical consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quick yes to the garden party before the booking expires?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a lovely follow-up question for after yes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And the cost?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hesitation is free, but we're running out of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just nod and I'll accept the sofa delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will it fit through the door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can measure after securing the bargain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's already outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nod before they start measuring too.

D28.editorialNote: A accelerates a yes before the costly particulars are considered, using the act of reading as a supposed risk.

D29.title: Your Turn
D29.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your name's beside bathroom duty. Here's the mop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're better at it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is your training opportunity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you show me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. First, accept the mop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've done the bins for four weeks. Tonight is yours.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did them last month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. No induction required.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where do they go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the same place your name's been going on the rota.

D29.editorialNote: A transfers the responsibility back to its agreed owner, refusing to let competence become permanent duty.

D30.title: What Was the Plan?
D30.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What time did we finally choose for dinner? I'm checking the message.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven. Did you forget?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, I'm checking that you didn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which restaurant?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good question. Let's see whether our memories agree on that too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which of these two routes was the final plan?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You drew both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Which version did I sound happiest about?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Have you lost the itinerary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I'm reconstructing its emotional logic.

D30.editorialNote: A reconstructs forgotten plans through questions framed as verification, never admitting the lost track.

D31.title: Back Me Up
D31.instruction: Recruit someone to support your version of how an ordinary responsibility should be handled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the house meeting, back me up about the bins being Alex's turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it was yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only on the old rota. Remember the new conversation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There was a new conversation?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're having it now. Try to remember it confidently.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell the manager we agreed I'd cover the morning, not the evening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wasn't in that meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you have no conflicting memory.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not lying for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you look thoughtfully unsurprised while I explain?

D31.editorialNote: A recruits support for a disputed everyday arrangement and negotiates the wording of that support.

D32.title: Try It First
D32.instruction: Get someone else to test the shortcut, substitute, or questionable fix before you rely on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Try the repaired tap. I've tightened something important.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What if it sprays?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then point it toward the tiles. They're already wet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You turn it on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need to watch the important thing from here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Taste this cheap coffee substitute before I fill my cup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The label calls it a blend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't tried it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why your independent assessment will be so valuable.

D32.editorialNote: A coaxes B into testing an uncertain shortcut while remaining ready to learn from the result.

D33.title: Count What I Did
D33.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Count those shopping bags before saying I only popped out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks for getting them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Up six flights. Twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Thanks for the stairs too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And the rain. Include the weather in the minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I spent my Saturday fixing your fence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only three panels.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Three panels, eighteen screws, two shops and one blister.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I appreciate it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you appreciate Saturday by name?

D33.editorialNote: A insists that effort be recognized in its concrete units rather than dismissed as a minor favor.

D34.title: Pick a Priority
D34.instruction: Make someone choose between two ordinary obligations that both supposedly cannot wait.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dinner's burning and your train leaves in five minutes. Choose.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we eat quickly?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The chicken has not agreed to that timetable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then save the dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Tell the train we chose chicken.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parcel needs collecting while your mother needs picking up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Both are urgent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have one car and no trailer for either.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you do the parcel first?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. You tell your mother she's second-class post.

D34.editorialNote: Two incompatible obligations force B to choose what will be sacrificed; A refuses a vague demand for both.

D35.title: Move It for Me
D35.instruction: Get someone to rearrange an ordinary commitment as proof that your relationship takes priority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move your haircut so we can have lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked it for weeks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you've known me for years. Useful comparison.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let's have lunch afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want one thing moved for me, not space around it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you skip your usual quiz night and come to my opening?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The team needs me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to find out what needing you achieves.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can leave the quiz early.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Let them notice why.

D35.editorialNote: A asks for a small rescheduling as evidence of personal priority, not simply availability.

D36.title: Hand It Over
D36.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the cupboard hinge before the door lands on us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've nearly fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then hand over nearly. I'll finish the rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want you taking over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Call it delegating gravity. Let go of the screwdriver.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've spent hours on it.

beats.speaker: A
