beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

D36.editorialNote: A seeks control of a task by offering a concrete handover while B keeps defending ownership.

D37.title: Put It Back Quietly
D37.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your umbrella's back in its usual place. Very ordinary sight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's been experiencing the weather privately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put it nearer the door. Better ventilation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the plate back. Lovely new flower pattern, isn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our plates were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Were they? This cupboard really changes the light.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's a price sticker underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How reassuring. We can finally insure it.

D37.editorialNote: A restores an object inconspicuously while new evidence threatens to reveal the original misuse.

D38.title: Talk Around the Mess
D38.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've polished one spoon beautifully. Admire that shine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The rest of the kitchen's filthy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why this spoon deserves encouragement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to clean everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's not overwhelm the spoon on its first success.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which label colour suits these boxes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You haven't packed them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good labels prevent moving-day confusion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The van's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'd better choose a colour the driver likes.

D38.editorialNote: A directs attention to minor presentable details so a major unfinished responsibility stays unaddressed.

D39.title: Spare Them the Hassle
D39.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enjoy your lunch. The bucket in the kitchen's just my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Water's coming through the ceiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've promoted the project to two buckets.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should I call someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've called. Finish your sandwich before the third bucket needs introducing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't worry about the repair bill. I've sorted it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is my bike on the invoice?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A minor detail of the sorting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How much was it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Less than the amount of your afternoon I'd lose explaining it.

D39.editorialNote: A hides an inconvenient problem to spare B worry and quietly increases their own burden.

D40.title: Who Changed It?
D40.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone uses it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The sofa's blocking the cupboard. Did it migrate overnight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I needed room for yoga.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So it had a guide.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Can its guide explain the cupboard's new opening hours?

D40.editorialNote: Innocent detail questions narrow responsibility for a changed shared plan until a voluntary admission becomes likely.

D41.title: Basically Finished
D41.instruction: Describe incomplete, late, or improvised work as a thoughtful version of completion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your cupboard is finished. I've chosen a handle-free design.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I open it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: By appreciating the uninterrupted surface first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It won't open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the storage is exceptionally secure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The report's complete apart from the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The numbers are the report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I've finished its supporting structure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's just a title page.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A clear vision. Most reports lack one.

D41.editorialNote: Incomplete work is described as an intentional finished product; practical testing exposes what remains absent.

D42.title: I’ve Done This Before
D42.instruction: Perform calm familiarity with the task while learning how it works from every new clue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've used this coffee machine plenty. You press here, naturally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the steam button.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, warming up before the main operation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put a cup underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I was checking you remembered the sequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This tent's familiar. The long pole goes across the top.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the groundsheet rod.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Testing the components.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've never pitched this model.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not with such an observant assistant.

D42.editorialNote: A learns from B's practical corrections while pretending to recall each step from experience.

D43.title: Outdo the Effort
D43.instruction: Answer every favor, chore, or sacrifice with a bigger one that restores your lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You brought dinner? I'll wash every dish in your house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only made soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll polish the soup spoons too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please just eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I repaint the dining room. It needs to match your kindness.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks for driving me. I'll cover your whole weekend shift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a ten-minute lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll do next weekend too. Such efficient generosity deserves scale.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's far too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We're finally ahead of the lift.

D43.editorialNote: A exceeds the actual favor just offered, turning generosity into competitive escalation.

D44.title: Efficiency Win
D44.instruction: Celebrate each inconvenience as proof that a faster, cheaper, or smarter routine can now be invented.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The lift's broken. We can cancel the gym and use the stairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We live eight floors up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A full programme included in the rent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do we carry the shopping?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Resistance training. We've saved two memberships.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The dishwasher broke. Let's all eat from one pan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We have guests.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Fewer introductions between courses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They'll want plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll serve sandwiches. This system keeps improving.

D44.editorialNote: A derives a concrete efficiency scheme from each inconvenience rather than celebrating without a plan.

D45.title: No Trouble at All
D45.instruction: Remain gracious and accommodating while making your growing inconvenience impossible to miss.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another guest? Lovely. I'll divide my dinner into an extra portion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you sure there's enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For everyone arriving, certainly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can bring food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No trouble. I've always wanted to know what hosting tastes like without eating.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll carry your bag. This shoulder's had a full life.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can take it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not now it's learned the weight of your hobbies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only books.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. My spine's becoming extremely well read.

D45.editorialNote: A accommodates each extra burden while ensuring the cost remains impossible to overlook.

D46.title: Fair Exchange
D46.instruction: Price every favor in time, effort, inconvenience, or future obligation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll wash up if you do two shopping trips.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two trips for one pan?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This pan has dried cheese. Rates have changed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll soak it first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then one trip and the detergent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thirty minutes helping you move buys me Saturday morning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Saturday's my only free morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll understand the value of my thirty minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I pay cash?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enough to buy back a Saturday. Let's calculate.

D46.editorialNote: The price of a favor is recalculated in concrete time and effort when B challenges the exchange.

D47.title: Technically, Yes
D47.instruction: Comply with every agreement in the narrowest possible way while insisting you honored it completely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've moved a box, as requested. Lovely working with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There are nineteen more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you now have experience requesting one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant all of them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good clarification. We'll price that as a new project.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I watered the plant you pointed at.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The others are wilting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You pointed very specifically.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant the plants generally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then next time use a wider finger.

D47.editorialNote: A fulfills the literal minimum of an agreement and treats B's broader expectation as a new request.

D48.title: One Thing Leads to Another
D48.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To fix this tap, we should replace the sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It only needs a washer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A new washer deserves reliable surroundings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sink's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need to ask why the kitchen makes it look tired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: This chair leg's loose. We should inspect all the chairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only that one wobbles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They share a manufacturer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The others passed your test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the table must be teaching it bad habits.

D48.editorialNote: A turns a small repair into a progressively larger intervention through a consistent chain of supposed dependencies.

S49.title: The Final Word
S49.instruction: Treat every opinion you offer as a ruling and every continued discussion as an appeal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We'll paint the hall green. That is my ruling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was thinking blue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your appeal has been received.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It wasn't an appeal. It was an opinion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it has no standing against the ruling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided we order soup.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're choosing our own lunches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An interesting challenge to jurisdiction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll have a sandwich.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Noted. The soup ruling remains on the record.

S49.editorialNote: Opinions become rulings and ordinary disagreement becomes a formal appeal.

S50.title: Conditional Command
S50.instruction: Project firm authority, then soften whenever the source of that authority might be questioned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All deliveries use my entrance from now on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who appointed you building supervisor?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can be flexible about the entrance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Is that badge signed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's not bury a good doorway policy in paperwork.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm setting the rehearsal order. Solos first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did the director ask you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She values initiative. We could begin with your solo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No need. An ensemble opening suddenly feels more inclusive.

S50.editorialNote: A retreats tactically when asked who authorized their power, then tries to preserve the appearance of command.

S51.title: The Gatekeeper
S51.instruction: Use expertise and standards to decide who is qualified to judge, participate, or proceed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before joining our cheese panel, identify this rind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just came to eat cheese.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Consumption is not qualification.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I ask why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the rind test. Questions shape the panel too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may judge the garden competition once I check your pruning certificate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a street competition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then a street-level certificate should suffice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who certified you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That question requires an advanced certificate.

S51.editorialNote: Participation depends on A's expert eligibility standard, which expands when B tries to discuss the standard itself.

S52.title: Rightful Place
S52.instruction: Carry yourself as the rightful holder of your role and treat any demand for proof as an insult.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Why is my name on the waiting list for my own table?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone has to book.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: People seeking a table book. I have a table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then those people are borrowing my problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my nameplate on the committee chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's an election first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An election confirms legitimacy. It doesn't invent my chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll need to nominate yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How insulting. The nameplate already has.

S52.editorialNote: A regards an ordinary proof requirement as an affront to a role they consider inherently theirs.

S53.title: The Crown Must Pass
S53.instruction: Treat another person as your likely successor. Prepare them to lead, then reclaim authority whenever their independence makes your influence feel temporary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's the café key. Your first day in charge. I'll watch quietly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm changing the opening hours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Run the quiet decisions past me first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said I was in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. I'm here to help you resemble it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Take my chair, deputy. Lead the meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First, let's remove the old approval process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent confidence. I'll need to approve that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the process I'm removing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your first lesson is tact around the chair's previous occupant.

S53.editorialNote: A prepares a successor but takes back control as soon as succession looks real.

S54.title: The Quiet Veto
S54.instruction: Remain pleasant and cooperative while behaving as though nothing can proceed without your private consent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd love your exhibition to happen. I haven't signed the room form yet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What needs changing?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring me something I can feel comfortable signing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said the plan was perfect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'd hate to spoil it with a premature signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your proposal has my wholehearted encouragement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we have the funding code?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As soon as encouragement becomes consent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's the difference?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six digits, which I'm still considering.

S54.editorialNote: A remains agreeable while withholding the concrete consent needed to proceed.

S55.title: We Started Equal
S55.instruction: Use shared beginnings to erase present rank, titles, and attempts to place distance between you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We started on the same biscuit-packing line. Pass the biscuits, Director.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please use my title at work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Fellow Biscuit Packer with an Office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Things have changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can afford to pass the expensive ones.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've pulled my chair level with yours. First-day habit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This side is for management.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We couldn't even find the toilets together on day one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm your manager now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then manage to remember where we both started.

S55.editorialNote: Shared beginnings erase present rank; A treats new formal distance as a betrayal of old equality.

S56.title: My Support, My Say
S56.instruction: Treat every past favor as a continuing investment in your right to influence present decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I funded your bakery mixer. I should help choose the new menu.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a birthday gift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To a particular vision of cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm making bread now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my investment needs a meeting with bread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before changing the club name, remember who paid the deposit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've paid you back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Financially. I'm discussing my continuing confidence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Does that ever get paid back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while decisions remain available.

S56.editorialNote: Past support is treated as an ongoing investment that purchases current decision-making rights.

S57.title: The Trusted Deputy
S57.instruction: Act as the reliable second-in-command, managing access and details while quietly shaping every decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've prepared the director's options. Mine is first, in larger print.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's steering the decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, assisting its visibility.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put them in alphabetical order.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. I've named mine 'A Sensible Beginning.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The captain's busy. I'll decide which messages reach her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This one changes our route.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it goes under 'things she needn't worry about.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She needs to know.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll summarise it after highlighting my preferred route.

S57.editorialNote: A controls a leader's choices through access and presentation while insisting they are merely assisting.

S58.title: The Succession Race
S58.instruction: Treat every success, mistake, and compliment as evidence in an ongoing contest over who should lead.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I fixed the office kettle. Useful evidence when they choose the next manager.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The manager isn't leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I have time to fix the toaster.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to campaign.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm simply maintaining the succession appliances.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sam forgot the meeting again. I've added it to my leadership comparison.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There isn't a leadership contest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my perfect attendance is comfortably ahead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm cancelling today's meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll record that I arrived for it anyway.

S58.editorialNote: Everyday outcomes become a succession dossier, even before any vacancy exists.

S59.title: Indispensable Rival
S59.instruction: Use another person’s judgment constantly while minimizing how much influence that dependence gives them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Check my speech for errors. Just a formality.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The central argument doesn't work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I suspected that. Confirm my suspicion more fully.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you credit me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For agreeing with my suspicion? That seems excessive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which route would you take? I already have a preference.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The east road. The west bridge is closed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly the kind of issue I was testing you on.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were heading west.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To inspect the closure before my eastward decision.

S59.editorialNote: A relies on a rival's judgment while denying the influence and taking public ownership.

S60.title: Once Undermined
S60.instruction: Treat every disagreement as a possible repeat of the moment your authority was previously weakened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You want to change the meeting time. That's how the last coup started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It clashed with lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Last time it clashed with my authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just hungry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then submit the hunger in writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called me Pat instead of Chairperson. Interesting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've known each other for years.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And last year you voted against my shed proposal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're discussing tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which I will now put to a recorded vote.

S60.editorialNote: A interprets small disagreement through a concrete past undermining, escalating procedural defenses.

S61.title: Power Looks Good
S61.instruction: Act fascinated by confident behavior; imitate it closely while resenting how naturally it seems to work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That pause of yours made everyone listen. I'll use a longer one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a cough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An authoritative cough. Mine will be deliberate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to copy me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Say that again. I like the certainty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You got the table just by raising an eyebrow. Must be nice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could ask the waiter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. I'm developing a stronger eyebrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's coming over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Watch mine outperform yours.

S61.editorialNote: A imitates another's confident technique while resenting its ease, visibly adjusting the same borrowed behavior.

S62.title: Formerly Important
S62.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've rung my old headteacher's bell. Why is nobody lining up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: This is your retirement lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lunch still benefits from orderly pupils.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're your former colleagues.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should require less supervision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the shop takings to me, as usual.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sold the shop last year.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I kept the counting tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That doesn't make you the owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why does the money still fit?

S62.editorialNote: An old office habit persists after the role ends; A treats lost power as a technical inconvenience.

S63.title: One Mistake from Gone
S63.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's my first lunch order as supervisor. Is soup too indecisive?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's just lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's what a confident supervisor would say.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Order what you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you witness that instruction before I risk the soup?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed the delivery form. Was my signature managerial enough?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It just needs to be legible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So they've lowered the standard for me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: No, it's the same form.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll practise until I deserve the same form.

S63.editorialNote: A treats a trivial new decision as proof of continued suitability and seeks escalating verification.

S64.title: Protection Has Terms
S64.instruction: Treat safety, support, and reassurance as arrangements that require you to remain in control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can borrow my car if I approve every stop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm visiting my sister.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A safe first destination. Send me the return plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I decide that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while enjoying my comprehensive support package.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll back your exhibition, provided I choose the guest list.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's controlling the exhibition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Protecting it from unsuitable viewers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's about independence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me make independence safe for you.

S64.editorialNote: Support is offered as a conditional arrangement that keeps A in supervisory control.

S65.title: Chosen by Power
S65.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. Should I join her table now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She says hello to everybody.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then she'll recognise me when you introduce us properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She doesn't know your name.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. There's still room for a memorable introduction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me beside the director in the group photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She only asked you to hold her coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A position of trust.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's taking it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then photograph the handover. It shows we work closely.

S65.editorialNote: A treats influential attention as proof of inclusion, trying to convert incidental contact into public affiliation.

S66.title: Public Respect
S66.instruction: Seek visible signs of respect and treat private appreciation as insufficient.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for your lovely private note. Which microphone will you repeat it into?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant it just for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I received it. Now we can broaden distribution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a staff lunch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A captive audience for the full title.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you use 'Chair' when introducing me at the picnic?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you're in charge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it won't confuse them to hear it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're passing sandwiches.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pass them through the Chair.

S66.editorialNote: Private appreciation is insufficient; A seeks a public, correctly framed display of respect.

S67.title: Chain of Command
S67.instruction: Treat every question, favor, and decision as something that must travel through the proper hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for a teaspoon must go through the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're standing beside the teaspoons.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Physical proximity is not authority.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the kitchen supervisor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then countersign your request. I'll pass it up to catering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I lend you this ladder, your department head must ask mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're neighbours, cleaning our gutters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need to establish departmental boundaries.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just borrow it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while the gutter committee remains unformed.

S67.editorialNote: An ordinary request is routed through an escalating hierarchy, not just used as an avoidance objective.

S68.title: Power Vacuum
S68.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's chairing this picnic. We can't open the hamper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can decide together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who authorises together?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just pass the bread.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is that a nomination? I accept.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The manager's left early. Who's responsible for the kettle?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Anyone can make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An uncontrolled beverage structure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll make it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Say it clearly so we have a chain of succession.

S68.editorialNote: An empty leadership position becomes the emergency; attempts at shared decisions create another authority question.

S69.title: Opportunity for Influence
S69.instruction: Find a path to greater influence in every assignment, setback, or unexpected responsibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've given me the broken printer. I'll need authority over purchasing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It probably just needs paper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll oversee paper policy too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a small repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. A manageable beginning for my department.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My proposal failed? Then I'll chair the review.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're not forming a committee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Someone must coordinate the absence of one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're getting more work, not more power.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll need a deputy.

S69.editorialNote: A turns each undesirable task or setback into a specific expansion of influence.

S70.title: Who Can Authorize This?
S70.instruction: Treat titles and speeches as secondary; focus on who can grant access, allocate resources, and create consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely ribbon-cutting speech. Who has the key to the building?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chief executive is over there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does she have the key?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then my congratulations can wait. I need the caretaker.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your title's impressive. Can you release the repair funds?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My deputy handles finance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then may I speak to the powerful part of this office?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I make the big decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Decide to introduce me to the cheque book.

S70.editorialNote: A ignores symbolic rank and follows the concrete power to unlock, pay or authorize.

S71.title: Symbol of Office
S71.instruction: Choose one symbol, privilege, or position and treat control of it as proof of legitimate authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm wearing the barbecue apron. I decide when the burgers turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my apron.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you should respect its office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That would be a transfer of power. Finish your petition first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I have the meeting bell. That means I'm chairing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a bicycle bell.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yet you stopped talking when I rang it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I borrow it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After I finish deciding whether you may.

S71.editorialNote: Possession of a small symbol becomes A's basis for legitimate authority, even when the symbol is trivial.

S72.title: Invisible Hierarchy
S72.instruction: Treat every interaction as evidence of an unseen hierarchy and keep identifying who truly outranks whom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fetched her coffee. So she's above you on the chart.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was being nice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Unpaid tribute. A very secure position for her.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She fetched mine yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is a rotating monarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everyone looked at the quiet man before agreeing. He must run this place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's the electrician. The lights flickered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Control over visibility. Higher than management.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's leaving now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we should conclude before the hierarchy goes dark.

S72.editorialNote: A reads an ordinary exchange as evidence of hidden rank and updates a hierarchy from each new clue.

D49.title: Make Them Your Deputy
D49.instruction: Get someone’s help by defining it as service under your direction.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I need help running the raffle. I've made you a deputy badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not co-organiser?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because I need help, not a second direction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What does the deputy do?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everything I can confidently delegate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Come organise the picnic as my second-in-command.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We could share the work equally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. You execute half; I direct all of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That isn't equal.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your first assignment is improving the wording.

D49.editorialNote: A secures help by inventing a subordinate role and preserves the hierarchy when B proposes equality.

D50.title: Not Dismissed
D50.instruction: Keep someone present by treating departure as a privilege only you can grant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shift ends at five. Your dismissal is still pending.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's five fifteen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. You've demonstrated punctual attendance at the dismissal review.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need to approve your change of location.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may collect your coat once I've finished with you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were only having coffee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And we're now concluding it formally.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The café's closing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll dismiss the café first.

D50.editorialNote: A treats a normal departure as a release they personally grant, continually redefining when that release applies.

D51.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
D51.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your apology should mention interrupting the chair, not just spilling the tea.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry about your trousers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The trousers hold no office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry I interrupted you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Chair.' Let's repair the title while we're here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You called my plan silly in front of the trainees.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry it didn't work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The plan failed privately. You disrespected me publicly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like an email?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With my position in the subject line.

D51.editorialNote: A redirects apology away from the practical incident toward the affront to A's rank.

D52.title: Secure the Endorsement
D52.instruction: Get a visible endorsement that makes your decision or position harder to challenge.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Would you endorse the new rota into this microphone?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I already said it was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quietly. Quietly can't protect me at the staff meeting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I email you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Copy everyone who might blame me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign here to say you support the extension.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like it, but I'd rather not put my name down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your support has no address when objections arrive.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I use initials?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if we print the key beside them.

D52.editorialNote: A seeks support in a public durable form that will survive later disagreement.

D53.title: Delegate Downward
D53.instruction: Make someone accept an unwanted responsibility by placing them lower in the hierarchy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As junior coordinator, you get the blocked sink.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I coordinated the whole event yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And today we develop your drainage leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You just don't want to do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Senior staff must remain available to delegate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The inspection notes go down the chain to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're all the complaints.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll gain a broad understanding of operations.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why do you keep the compliments?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They require a senior signature.

D53.editorialNote: An unwanted task is assigned as proof of junior rank, and every objection is reframed as a developmental duty.

D54.title: Find the Real Authority
D54.instruction: Probe until you know who can approve, block, or reverse the outcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everybody's approved the trip. Who can still cancel it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The committee signed unanimously.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whose phone call would make us tear that up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The treasurer controls the deposit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Where's the treasurer?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which signature actually releases this repair money?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All three are important.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which one could undo the other two?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance can freeze it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take my broken pipe to finance.

D54.editorialNote: A follows authority past titles to the person who can actually stop or reverse the decision.

D55.title: Build a Coalition
D55.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit on my side for the shed vote. It'll show broad support.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm undecided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sit broadly undecided beside me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That would look like agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. You understand the seating plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: May I put your name on the petition?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't read it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pencil, then. Provisional solidarity.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's it about?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First let's get enough names for it to seem worth reading.

D55.editorialNote: A builds visible support before agreement is settled, bargaining down from endorsement to appearance.

D56.title: Challenge by Proxy
D56.instruction: Persuade someone else to challenge a rule or authority before you risk doing it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the director why the overtime rule changed. I'll support you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why don't you ask?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your fresh perspective won't carry my disciplinary history.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand beside me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just behind. Where supportive people remain employable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You should question the queue-jumping policy at the club.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You hate it too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which gives me excellent notes for your speech.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put your name on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll hold the notes. That's practically a signature.

D56.editorialNote: A recruits a proxy challenge and carefully negotiates how visible their own support will be.

D57.title: Use the Proper Title
D57.instruction: Make someone acknowledge your standing through a title, privilege, courtesy, or public sign of respect.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me as Director Patel, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Certainly, Pat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've removed the working part.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a barbecue.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then announce it over the sausages: Director Patel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My place card should say Chairperson, not simply Jo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone knows you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then nobody will struggle with the extra word.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no room on the card.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the larger plate.

D57.editorialNote: A insists on a specific courtesy and escalates from a missed word to a visible status marker.

D58.title: Declare Allegiance
D58.instruction: Make someone choose which person, side, or claim to authority they will support.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Are you backing my proposal or Morgan's?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like parts of both.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whose name goes above your favourite parts?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why choose a side?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because the meeting only has two sides of the table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wear my campaign ribbon for the club election.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm staying neutral.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which campaign asked you to stay neutral?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Neither.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mine has an excellent vacancy.

D58.editorialNote: A turns partial agreement or neutrality into a demand to choose whose authority to support.

D59.title: Obey Without Explanation
D59.instruction: Create increasingly inconvenient requests that test whether someone accepts your authority.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring that empty box to my desk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What do you need it for?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At present, to establish whether you'll bring it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Take it back without the question this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stand beside the window while I check something.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What are you checking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Whether the instruction needs an explanation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's cold over here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then close the window and remain instructional.

D59.editorialNote: Trivial tasks become increasingly inconvenient tests of obedience; A refuses to supply a practical reason.

D60.title: Pass Me the Authority
D60.instruction: Get someone to transfer authority publicly by naming you as the person who decides what happens next.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand me the hall key and tell everyone I'm now in charge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I just give you the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The door will understand. The committee needs words.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They know you're taking over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let them hear you stop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before leaving the meeting, name me as the person who decides.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're sitting in my chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Furniture announces location, not succession.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine. You're chairing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: To the room, please. I already agree.

D60.editorialNote: A seeks a public transfer of decision-making, not merely possession of a useful object.

D61.title: Orders from the Shadows
D61.instruction: Hide that you set the problem in motion while quietly directing how everyone responds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's fix the delivery mix-up. Send the crates back through my office.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your email sent them to the wrong city.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which means I know the route intimately.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Should we show the manager the email?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Show them my corrected routing chart first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody panic about the cancelled bookings. I'll direct the recovery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ordered the cancellations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then consistency demands I order the next step too.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why did you cancel them?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That question isn't recovering any bookings. Call this number.

D61.editorialNote: A conceals their original instruction while steering the response with suspiciously precise knowledge.

D62.title: Not Up for Debate
D62.instruction: Keep the conversation from examining where your authority comes from or whether it is legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before questioning my appointment, finish the stock check.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Who appointed you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stock first. Governance afterward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I see the letter?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can I see the stock? Only one is running out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My badge authorises this inspection. Open the cupboard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's no signature on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Signatures are tomorrow's administrative focus.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you make the badge?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're inspecting cupboards, not stationery.

D62.editorialNote: A diverts scrutiny from the source of authority into urgent work under that authority.

D63.title: For Stability’s Sake
D63.instruction: Hide a destabilizing truth because you believe the current balance of power must be protected.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The director's unavailable. Let's keep today's launch exactly as planned.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Her office is empty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A distraction-free leadership environment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has she resigned?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The launch still has a time. Let's protect that certainty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've shortened the committee briefing so we can get through the fair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where's the treasurer's page?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It would complicate the cake stall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are we out of money?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We still have cakes. Let's discuss what can sell.

D63.editorialNote: A withholds destabilising information to preserve collective function rather than personal innocence.

D64.title: Name Your Backers
D64.instruction: Get someone to reveal who supports their position, who authorized it, and who benefits from it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who supported your decision to close the workshop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I signed it myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who made it comfortable to sign?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The director was consulted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Whose budget improves when the workshop disappears?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your proposal says 'we recommend.' Who's we?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The planning group.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which member would defend it if the roof falls in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Finance pushed for the cheaper option.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then put finance beside the word recommend.

D64.editorialNote: A seeks the coalition behind a decision, using specific accountability questions to reveal backers.

D65.title: Strategic Retreat
D65.instruction: Describe every loss of control as a deliberate concession made from strength.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've generously surrendered the chair's role.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You lost the election.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave democracy room to flourish.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're removing your nameplate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Space for my influence to become less obvious.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've chosen to withdraw my exhibition proposal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The gallery rejected it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They correctly anticipated my next move.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They rejected the appeal too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A remarkably well-coordinated retreat.

D65.editorialNote: A describes an actual loss as voluntary strategic generosity and reframes each visible setback as chosen space.

D66.title: Act Authorized
D66.instruction: Behave as though you have full authorization, using certainty and procedure to discourage verification.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm cleared to inspect the storeroom. Here's my pass.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's unsigned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approval has moved beyond handwriting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call the manager.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her the inspection's reached the telephone stage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've stamped my request. The room's booked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's your own stamp.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. A direct approval chain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't authorise yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll need to discuss why the stamp says approved.

D66.editorialNote: A behaves as though authorization is settled and treats missing evidence as an advanced form of approval.

D67.title: Rank Everything
D67.instruction: Turn every new contribution into a ranking that places you nearer the top.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ranked our picnic contributions. Planning outranks sandwiches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I also drove everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Transport comes below destination selection. Mine again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Do we need a ranking?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Questioning the ranking scores low on teamwork.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your suggestion is useful. I'll put it below my strategic overview.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My suggestion fixed the problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A practical achievement inside my strategic problem recognition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You caused the problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'm foundational to the whole project.

D67.editorialNote: A ranks each new contribution so their own work moves toward the top.

D68.title: More Power, More Problems
D68.instruction: Celebrate every burden, restriction, or crisis as evidence that your influence is expanding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've given me three more departments to cover. My influence is soaring.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've cut your budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They trust me to transcend money.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've also lost your office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. My reach is no longer confined by walls.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another complaint for me! I'm becoming central to everything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're complaining about you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Direct public engagement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They want you removed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A strong mandate to discuss my position.

D68.editorialNote: Each added burden or loss is celebrated as evidence of growing influence.

D69.title: Gracious Command
D69.instruction: Remain warm and appreciative while steadily reducing everyone else’s room to choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for choosing the venue. I've narrowed it to my garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I preferred the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A lovely contribution. We'll use its name for a garden table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: So I don't choose?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've helped us appreciate how much simpler this is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm so grateful you're helping. I've assigned your whole weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I offered an hour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Such generosity deserves room to grow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not available Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for clarifying. Saturday will be delightfully full.

D69.editorialNote: Warm appreciation accompanies shrinking options until disagreement itself is reframed as helpful cooperation.

D70.title: Access Has a Price
D70.instruction: Turn every piece of access, information, or approval into a favor, debt, or condition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll open the storeroom in return for a favour.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only need a mop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it should be a modest favour. I'll name it later.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't I borrow the key?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a second level of membership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can introduce you to the curator if you support my exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Couldn't you just introduce us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I could. What a valuable ability.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What support do you need?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now we're near the gallery entrance.

D70.editorialNote: A prices access or information as a future obligation, making the exchange concrete.

D71.title: Consensus Means Me
D71.instruction: Treat every partial agreement as confirmation that everyone has accepted your leadership.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You nodded at Friday. I'll announce unanimous support for my plan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I agreed to Friday, not the plan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We've approved the timetable of my leadership.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I object to the budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll announce unanimous calendar support first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You like the blue poster? Good, the campaign has consensus.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I dislike the slogan.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: But its surroundings have your confidence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't say I endorse it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll say you helped establish the visual direction under me.

D71.editorialNote: A converts limited agreement into consent to leadership while downplaying explicit objections.

D72.title: Expand Your Jurisdiction
D72.instruction: Use every new problem as a reason to expand what you are entitled to control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The kitchen supplies my team's tea. I need a kitchen key.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You manage accounts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Accounts require alertness. Tea controls alertness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Where does that end?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The roof leaks on the kettle. I'll need that key too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your delivery delays affect my schedule. I'll oversee transport.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You only book meeting rooms.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: People travel to rooms. It's one system.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you manage the roads next?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only the ones leading to my rooms.

D72.editorialNote: Every practical connection becomes grounds to expand A's control into a new area.

S73.title: Emotional Seniority
S73.instruction: Carry yourself as the person who understands this relationship best, and treat your interpretation as the one that should settle disagreements.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know why we're arguing about the spare key. We're afraid of change.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm afraid of you losing another key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how change expresses itself through you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just return it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: See? You're trying to close the emotional door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our dinner silence means we're comfortable together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm angry about your joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You only tell me that because you're comfortable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please stop interpreting me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An honest request. Our communication's improving.

S73.editorialNote: A claims authority over what the relationship means and treats B's contrary account as evidence within A's interpretation.

S74.title: Keeper of the Peace
S74.instruction: Project calm authority over the relationship while carefully avoiding anything that might expose how fragile the peace really is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've made soup. We can have a perfectly calm dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We need to discuss last night.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After soup. Nothing sharp while we're using spoons.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hand is shaking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The soup's excited. I'm managing both of us beautifully.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's put the difficult letter under the fruit bowl until Sunday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's Sunday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Next Sunday. A full week of peace.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can't keep postponing this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then speak softly. I've balanced the bowl very carefully.

S74.editorialNote: A stages calm rituals to contain a fragile peace; a practical disturbance reveals the strain.

S75.title: I Know Your Tells
S75.instruction: Use intimate knowledge of habits, moods, and patterns as expertise that lets you diagnose every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tapped your cup three times. You're about to ask for money.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm waiting for the tea to cool.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the story you used before the bicycle loan.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't need money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then this is a much larger favour. I'll put the kettle back on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You chose the chipped mug. Bad news, isn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my favourite mug.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Especially before an uncomfortable sentence.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I just want tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the sentence before the sentence. I know your structure.

S75.editorialNote: A diagnoses personal habits as intimate evidence and expands the diagnosis when B denies the reading.

S76.title: Still Part of This
S76.instruction: Act as though shared history permanently guarantees your place, even when present boundaries suggest otherwise.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've hung my coat on my old hook. What's for dinner?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You moved out three years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The hook didn't.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We use that space for guests now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the guests their hook has an owner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my usual chair at the club table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your membership expired.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our history didn't. This chair remembers me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll need to reapply.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For what? Returning to where I already belong?

S76.editorialNote: A treats old membership as permanent entitlement despite present boundaries, keeping the same concrete place in dispute.

S77.title: Keeper of Precedent
S77.instruction: Treat your longer memory as an archive, not a throne. Cite specific promises and precedents whenever the relationship faces a new choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our Tuesday agreement says whoever cooks doesn't wash up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I didn't know you kept it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We both signed beside the spaghetti stain.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we change the rule?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Certainly. Together, before I cook again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We promised to call before borrowing the car. Here's the note.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: People change.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let's update the promise with both people present.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you'd forgotten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why I date things. Memory shouldn't decide fairness.

S77.editorialNote: A cites specific shared promises as evidence to renegotiate, not as automatic superiority.

S78.title: Private Access
S78.instruction: Use shared confidences and private knowledge as quiet leverage, never stating how much influence that closeness gives you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before the guests arrive, we should discuss the envelope in my drawer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Say it here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not beside your lovely public version of last summer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What are you implying?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only that we should take our tea somewhere quieter.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've still got the key to our old keepsake box.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why mention that at dinner?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I thought you'd prefer a mention to an opening.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put the key away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. Shall we talk in the kitchen first?

S78.editorialNote: Private knowledge gives A leverage without stating the secret; B's public setting intensifies that control.

S79.title: Our Private Language
S79.instruction: Use old references, shorthand, and familiar rhythms as proof that this connection exists beneath whatever has changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Purple umbrellas, remember? That's our signal for leaving a dull party.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought it meant order dessert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only with the eyebrow. Watch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That still means dessert.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We'll escape after pudding, like always.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two taps on the table. You know what that means.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We haven't done that since school.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your hand nearly answered.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was moving my glass.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move it twice and I'll get our coats.

S79.editorialNote: A revives a specific private shorthand and uses B's partial recall to restore shared rhythm.

S80.title: I Was There
S80.instruction: Treat your presence during a difficult time as an enduring claim on loyalty, honesty, and consideration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I sat beside you all night when the business failed. Tell me the real answer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said I'm fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At four in the morning you used shorter lies.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't have to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. That's why I'd like more than the visitor version now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I drove through that storm for you. Don't give me the polite refusal.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm genuinely busy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me what with. I earned a noun.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was years ago.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The road's repaired. My expectation of honesty hasn't.

S80.editorialNote: A's presence during a past difficulty becomes a claim to present honesty and loyalty.

S81.title: Back in Our Roles
S81.instruction: Return immediately to the role you usually play in this relationship, even when the present situation calls for something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're upset. I'll make tea and telephone whoever needs sorting out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just listen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Who am I listening about?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody needs fixing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll fix the temperature of the tea while you explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're late again. I've prepared your usual excuse.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was going to apologise honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll tidy the wording.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can do this myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me what my part is before you start.

S81.editorialNote: A resumes the familiar fixer or caretaker role even when B asks for a different kind of presence.

S82.title: The Other Favorite
S82.instruction: Treat every sign of attention, trust, and affection as something to compare with what another connection appears to receive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sam's photo has a bigger frame than mine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a bigger photograph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So you had room for more Sam.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can buy matching frames.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only if mine doesn't look like compensation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Their invitation has a ribbon. Mine has a staple.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ran out of ribbon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At exactly my place in the affection queue.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were the first invitation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why did you start with stationery instead of love?

S82.editorialNote: A compares concrete signs of affection and turns innocent practical explanations into further comparisons.

S83.title: Old Reflex
S83.instruction: Turn to this person first whenever uncertainty appears, as an old reflex. Notice the habit only after you have already involved them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which key opens my new flat? Sorry, you haven't been there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You chose it without me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. Which pocket would I have put the key in?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your left, usually.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There it is. We still work on the smaller decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've called to ask which coat to wear. You're already beside me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't need to call me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My thumb got worried before I did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wear the blue one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thanks. I'll hang up and tell you how it went.

S83.editorialNote: A seeks the familiar person's help reflexively and only notices the habit afterward.

S84.title: Almost Forgiven
S84.instruction: Behave as though the past is nearly resolved, but let each small disappointment reopen one precise part of the hurt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've forgiven the missed birthday. Pass the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then why is that date circled?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For administrative closure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've circled next year's too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Forgiveness benefits from advance notice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're fine about the broken vase. Don't make that particular joke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The vase joke?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The one where my disappointment is the amusing bit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we'd moved on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We had. You brought the vase with us.

S84.editorialNote: A claims forgiveness but a small related cue reopens a precise unreconciled detail.

S85.title: Easy to Love
S85.instruction: Interpret another person’s ease with affection as both admirable and unfair, then compete to seem equally worth choosing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everyone hugs you so easily. I've brought your favourite biscuits.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You didn't have to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Neither did they hug you, apparently. It just happens.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come sit with us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. I rehearsed a very spontaneous smile.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your greeting makes people light up. Listen to my new version.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Just say hello normally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hello! Was that effortlessly lovable?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was loud.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll reduce the volume and keep the affection.

S85.editorialNote: A envies easy affection and tries to match it through effort disguised as natural warmth.

S86.title: Who We Used to Be
S86.instruction: Perform the version of yourself that belonged to this relationship before it changed, and treat old chemistry as still recoverable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put on our old driving song. Shall we take the coast road?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We used to get lost there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, but I was adventurous then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You complained for forty miles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With chemistry. Let me try the opening complaint.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wore the scarf from our first photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't fit your coat anymore.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It fits the person you met.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You don't have to be that person.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just until dessert. He knew how to make you laugh.

S86.editorialNote: A performs their old relational self and tries to make past chemistry briefly usable in the present.

S87.title: One Step from Distance
S87.instruction: Treat pauses, divided attention, and small boundaries as signs that the connection may be slipping away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You took longer to answer my message today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was in a meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A meeting I used to hear about.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was just work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell me one boring detail so I know there's still room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said maybe to Friday. Should I stop setting your place?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to check my shift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm trying not to turn maybe into distance.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll tell you tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could tomorrow have a time?

S87.editorialNote: Small delays or boundaries are interpreted as incremental loss of connection rather than final disaster.

S88.title: Love Means Checking
S88.instruction: Treat close monitoring of choices, moods, and details as care, becoming more involved whenever you feel uncertain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Text me when you arrive, then when you've found your seat.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only the cinema.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Dark rooms deserve accurate updates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can look after myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Text me when you've started doing that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've packed your bag and checked your route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You packed things I don't need.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're protected against needs you haven't noticed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please stop checking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me you're safe and I'll check whether I can.

S88.editorialNote: Monitoring is framed as care and expands as B attempts to reassure A.

S89.title: Still Your Person
S89.instruction: Seek small signs that you remain special, trusted, and included without directly asking where you stand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Should I use my chipped mug or one of the guest cups?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Whichever you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I used to know without asking.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chipped one's still yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. I'll leave it beside yours, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've still got you as my emergency contact.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine like paperwork, or fine like you'd come?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd come.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll stop hovering over the delete button.

S89.editorialNote: A asks obliquely whether ordinary signs of special inclusion remain available.

S90.title: Remember What I Meant
S90.instruction: Create openings for shared memories that prove your past presence mattered and still deserves acknowledgment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've kept the little boat I made you. Remember that afternoon?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were by the lake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who stayed in the rain finding the right twig?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You did.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. The boat's getting credit, but I like a mention too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's my sleeve in your graduation photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You caught me when I tripped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Funny how the sleeve made the official album.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember the person in it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me that bit. The sleeve's heard enough.

S90.editorialNote: A invites a specific shared memory that acknowledges their past contribution and continued significance.

S91.title: Our Thing
S91.instruction: Protect one shared ritual, phrase, or tradition as the living proof that the relationship still exists.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Two spoons for dessert. We still do our thing.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we discuss the contract?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the first shared bite. Contracts shouldn't eat alone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ordered my own pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then bring it here. Our thing can expand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We haven't finished the old handshake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the last move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll slow down until your hand remembers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're keeping the taxi waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The taxi hasn't known us as long as this handshake.

S91.editorialNote: A shared ritual becomes proof of an ongoing relationship; practical business cannot proceed until it is honored.

S92.title: This Is How It Ends
S92.instruction: Treat every awkward pause, changed plan, or small disagreement as the possible beginning of permanent distance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You cancelled lunch. Should I leave my key?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have a dentist appointment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch, then the key, then separate dentists.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep your key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For emergencies or belonging? I'm choosing which ring it goes on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've moved my chair away from yours. Shall I pack the books too?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was vacuuming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's how empty spaces begin.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll move it back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before or after deciding which spaces stay empty?

S92.editorialNote: A reads a minor changed plan as the first step of permanent separation and begins practical farewell behavior.

S93.title: A Sign We’re Fine
S93.instruction: Interpret every laugh, favor, and familiar habit as evidence that the connection is stronger than appearances suggest.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered my chipped plate. We're still us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the only clean plate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And it found its way to me. Good instincts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're reading into it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd rather read into a plate than give up over washing-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We laughed at the same terrible joke. That's promising.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was just a joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. No effort, no negotiation, still together on the punchline.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We still need to talk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over dinner? The joke's earned us a table.

S93.editorialNote: A treats ordinary familiar gestures as reassuring evidence even when B offers a mundane explanation.

S94.title: Relationship Maintenance
S94.instruction: Accept every emotional complication, then focus on the next concrete act that could make staying connected easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can be angry and still choose a Tuesday to talk.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A diary won't fix this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. It gives the fixing somewhere to happen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't know what I'll say.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll start at six with not knowing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I accept that visiting is difficult. Shall I leave a spare key?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's not about the door.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Let's remove one easier obstacle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We still need boundaries.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then write the hours beside the key.

S94.editorialNote: A accepts emotional complexity and translates it into a manageable concrete act of connection.

S95.title: Those Exact Words
S95.instruction: Choose one phrase from the interaction and keep returning to what its wording must reveal about the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You wrote 'welcome for now.' Why for now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant you're welcome to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then now has brought an unnecessary suitcase.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're reading too much into it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Too much is another interesting measurement of my welcome.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said we're still friends. Still?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Friends.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can't quietly remove the word after I've heard it.
